title: Dealings in Shares (Securities) Policy

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Has the meaning given in Accounting Standard AASB 124 Related Party Disclosures. Bound by the prohibited-period ban (cl 1), may seek the Chairman's exceptional-circumstances approval to deal during a prohibited period (cl 3), and needs the Chairman's consent to deal at any other time outside the open trading window (cl 4(a)(ii)(1)).

tiers.name: employee
tiers.description: Employees who are not Key Management Personnel. Clause 1's prohibited-period ban is drafted to name only Key Management Personnel; under clause 4 an employee may deal freely only in the open trading window, and otherwise needs the consent of the Managing Director or the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company. Must notify the Company Secretary of the acquisition or disposal of any GUD security, or on ceasing to be a Director, so the Company can notify the ASX under Listing Rule 3.19A (Appendix 3X/3Y/3Z).

windows.start_anchor: 15th of the month in which the Company's financial year-end occurs
windows.end_anchor: one (1) day after release of the Company's financial statements for that year end, to the ASX

windows.start_anchor: 15th of the month in which the Company's interim financial half-year-end occurs
windows.end_anchor: one (1) day after release of the Company's interim financial statements for that half year, to the ASX

windows.start_anchor: one (1) day after release of information of a financial nature to the ASX
windows.end_anchor: thirty (30) days after release of information of a financial nature to the ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board, by resolution, may determine any other period as a 'prohibited period' (cl 1(c)), and may determine further 'excluded trading' categories notified to the ASX. The Policy does not state whether a Board-imposed additional prohibited period is confidential.

rules.detail: The Policy nowhere defines 'Dealing' or 'Securities' and never mentions derivatives, options over the underlying, or financial products created over GUD securities; it only regulates dealing 'in any GUD security'.
No reference to hedging, or to limiting the economic risk of unvested or vested equity incentive securities, appears anywhere in the document.
Prepaid forwards, collars or other monetisation structures are not named, and there is no dealing definition broad enough to expressly sweep them in.
Short selling is not mentioned; only acquisition and disposal of GUD securities held are addressed.
Securities lending is not referenced anywhere in the Policy.
Contracts for difference are not named and there is no financial-product definition that would catch them.
Margin loans are not mentioned; the Policy contains no restriction on using GUD securities as collateral.
Granting a charge, lien or other security interest over GUD securities is not addressed; the statutory summary of s1043A refers only to 'apply for, acquire or dispose of' securities.
No secured financing arrangement, of any kind, in respect of GUD securities is named or restricted.
There is no minimum holding period or anti-flipping intention test; the only timing restrictions are the prohibited periods and the open trading window.

clearance.approver: Chairman (Managing Director, if the Key Management Person concerned is the Chairman)
clearance.evidence: if that person is a Key Management Person or their associate, during any period which is not a prohibited period or a period referred to in clause 4(a)i. of this Policy, with the consent of the Chairman

clearance.approver: Managing Director or the Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: if that person is an employee or an associate of an employee (not being a Key Management Person), during any period which is not a prohibited period or a period referred to in clause 4(a)i. of this Policy, with the consent of the Managing Director or the Company Secretary.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (who notifies the ASX under Listing Rule 3.19A via Appendix 3X/3Y/3Z)
clearance.section: Director's Obligation on Acquisition or Disposal of Securities or on Ceasing to be a Director
clearance.evidence: a Director must notify the Company Secretary of the acquisition or disposal of any GUD security and the Company is obliged to notify the ASX (LR 3.19A).

exceptions.approver: Chairman (Managing Director, if the Key Management Person concerned is the Chairman)
exceptions.evidence: exceptional circumstances includes severe financial hardship, court order or court enforceable undertaking, or other exceptional circumstances determined by resolution of the Board

exceptions.approver: Chairman (Managing Director, if the Key Management Person concerned is the Chairman)
exceptions.evidence: exceptional circumstances includes severe financial hardship, court order or court enforceable undertaking, or other exceptional circumstances determined by resolution of the Board
exceptional circumstances includes ... other exceptional circumstances determined by resolution of the Board

external_documents: Disclosure Agreement between each Director and the Company (supplying acquisition/disposal information for ASX Appendix 3X/3Y/3Z notices under Listing Rule 3.19A)
exemption_authority: The Chairman (Managing Director, if the requesting Key Management Person is the Chairman) has complete discretion to approve dealing during a prohibited period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or enforceable undertaking, or other Board-determined circumstances), for a period not exceeding one month, on a written request stating the nature and extent of the proposed dealing and supporting evidence. The Board may also determine further excluded trading categories, notified to the ASX.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy prohibits Key Management Personnel from dealing 'in any GUD security' but never defines 'deal', 'Dealing' or 'Securities', and does not mention derivatives, hedging, margin lending, short selling, securities lending, CFDs, encumbrance or secured financing anywhere in the document.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because no defined term expressly sweeps in an OTC put/call or the loan securing it, the collar and its financing are not expressly prohibited, but nor is there any clearance pathway calibrated to them, so the bank should obtain the Company's written confirmation of treatment rather than rely on the Policy's silence.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel of the Company must not deal in any GUD security during the following periods ('prohibited periods')
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The absolute closed-period ban is drafted to bind only Key Management Personnel; if the collar counterparty is a non-KMP senior employee the closed period is not literally an outright bar on them, though clause 4 never blesses dealing by anyone during a prohibited period absent exceptional-circumstances approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: if that person is a Key Management Person or their associate, during any period which is not a prohibited period or a period referred to in clause 4(a)i. of this Policy, with the consent of the Chairman
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside the open 30-day post-results trading window, dealing (if the collar were treated as a dealing) needs the Chairman's prior consent for KMP, or Managing Director/Company Secretary consent for other employees, even when no prohibited period is in effect.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Chairman has complete discretion in deciding whether or not approval is to be given, and the period (not to exceed one month) in which the dealing may occur
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If entry, unwind or physical settlement of a collar had to occur during a prohibited period under exceptional-circumstances relief, the approved execution window cannot exceed one month.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a Director must notify the Company Secretary of the acquisition or disposal of any GUD security and the Company is obliged to notify the ASX (LR 3.19A). ... Each Director is required to enter into a Disclosure Agreement with the Company to supply such information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director entering into, unwinding, or having shares called away under a collar must notify the Company Secretary for an Appendix 3Y announcement, giving the market visibility of the derivative and loan structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the insider must not (whether as principal or agent) apply for, acquire or dispose of, or enter into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of any such securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Independent of the Policy's silence on derivatives, entering the collar while in possession of inside information remains a criminal and civil contravention under Corporations Act s1043A, with penalties up to $1.11 million for an individual noted in the document.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other period determined by resolution of the Board ... any other circumstances determined by the Board and notified to the ASX
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Board retains open-ended authority to impose extra blackout periods or bless further excluded trading categories, so the Company could add or remove flexibility for a collar at its discretion; the Policy does not say whether a Board-imposed additional prohibited period is confidential before it binds a director.

summary: GUD's Policy is a bare closed-period and consent regime that never mentions derivatives, hedging, margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing, so a funded OTC collar (purchased put, written call, and a loan secured on the collared vested shares) is not expressly prohibited. However, 'deal' and 'GUD security' are left undefined, so there is no confirmation that entering such a derivative and loan package would even be treated as a 'dealing' requiring compliance, leaving real interpretive risk. If treated as a dealing, it could occur freely in the open trading window (day 1 to day 30 after a relevant ASX financial release) subject only to not holding inside information, or otherwise only with the Chairman's consent for Key Management Personnel (Managing Director/Company Secretary consent for other employees); dealing during a formal prohibited period is barred outright save for Chairman-approved exceptional circumstances capped at one month. A director must separately notify the Company Secretary of the transaction for ASX Appendix 3Y disclosure, and the general insider trading prohibition under s1043A applies throughout regardless of the Policy's silence. On balance a funded collar is achievable if executed in an open window (or with the requisite consent) while not in possession of inside information, but the bank should seek the Company's written confirmation of how it characterises the collar and loan given the Policy gives no express answer.
